headline: Software growth lifts revenue, margins and cash flow slip
summary_short: IBM's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 1.1% y/y to $17.162 billion as Software grew 5% (Red Hat +11%) while Infrastructure fell 7% on a 42% IBM Z decline; net income fell 1.3% to $2.165 billion and diluted EPS fell 1.7% to $2.27, while free cash flow dropped 10.7% y/y to $2.540 billion.
summary_long: Software revenue grew 5% (Red Hat +11%, Data +19%) while Infrastructure fell 7% as IBM Z dropped 42% against a 37% surge in Distributed Infrastructure; Consulting was flat. Gross margin fell 1.0pt y/y to 57.7% on the mix shift. Net income fell 1% to $2.165B and diluted EPS fell 2% to $2.27, as pre-tax margin slipped to 14.4% from 15.3%, partly offset by a lower 12.6% effective tax rate. Cash fell to $7.2B from $13.6B at year-end after $10.5B of first-half acquisitions; long-term debt rose to $56.2B. IBM updated full-year constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 4-5% and reaffirmed its roughly $1 billion y/y free-cash-flow growth target.

drivers.explanation: Software revenue rose 5% led by Red Hat (+11%) and Data (+19%), and Financing rose 12%, while Infrastructure fell 7% as IBM Z dropped 42% against Distributed Infrastructure's 37% growth; the CFO cited 'revenue headwinds late in the second quarter.'
Net income fell 1% y/y as pre-tax income margin compressed to 14.4% from 15.3%, partially offset by a lower effective tax rate of 12.6% versus 15.5% a year ago.
EPS fell 2% as the 1% net income decline was compounded by a higher diluted share count of 953.3M versus 948.0M a year ago.
Adjusted EBITDA rose to $4.8B from $4.7B as pre-tax margin gains on an operating (non-GAAP) basis (19.2% vs 18.8%) offset the GAAP margin decline.

Free cash flow fell $0.3B y/y to $2.540B; the release attributes discipline in productivity and cash generation but does not itemize the specific cause of the quarterly decline beyond the change in operating cash and capex.

Cash fell to $7.2B from $13.6B at year-end after $10.5B invested in acquisitions during the first half of 2026; long-term debt rose to $56.2B. CEO Krishna cited AI-driven demand across software and a nearly $500 million Power/Storage order backlog as growth drivers going forward.
